directionalFollowup.correction: The files named atmosphere-west-before/after are actually a roughly northeast low-horizon view reconstructed from manual drag angles, not a west-facing sample. Their same-view (80,400) RGB changed from [116,149,190] to [105,145,197] after spatial weighting, reducing broad non-solar whitening. The file names are retained as historical artifacts; do not treat them as west evidence.
directionalFollowup.nearSunIntermediate: After turning to roughly the report Sun azimuth 268.821 degrees at local 18:00, the intermediate shader produced a visible solar disc and pale-yellow low western horizon; at 18:30 it produced an over-saturated red band. This failure drove below-horizon warm fade and forward-lobe exposure changes. The screenshots before the last patch are diagnostic, not current acceptance evidence.
directionalFollowup.finalIteration: The final shader iteration was viewed in the source WEAPP DevTools at one held manual camera and local 18:00, 18:30 and 19:30. At (80,400) RGB was [130,138,138], [51,64,82], [9,13,23] respectively; at (350,550) it was [236,226,201], [96,101,100], [9,13,23]. The 18:30 saturated red band does not appear in this held view and 19:30 stars return, but this camera differs from the intermediate over-red west view. The 18:00 low horizon remains pale/overbright; the last patch did not receive a controlled exact near-Sun close-view acceptance comparison. Do not claim that the original red view is fixed. This remains an illustrative directional trial, not calibrated sky appearance.
